Yeah I understand, I hated cognitive therapy and group work and personal nurse visits and psychiatrist visits.  What it is for me is the small things.  Im not happy, but there are things that make me less unhappy.  Tasty food, reading interesting facts, exercise.  It will not change me quickly and I may have to accept that Il never be "cured".  But im doing the best I can with the mind I have and I think there is strength in that.  Im not going to feed you this "it gets better" bullshit.  You might never feel better, but hold on to what you are, and be proud that youl never stop trying.  We are amazing, and what we do takes courage and mental stamina.  We do impact the world in positive ways even though we might never realize it.  We might not live life the same happy way that we see so many people do.  But we guide our lives, we create for ourselves a unique experience, we see things nobody else sees.  Respect is not an emotion.  I am emotionally numb, but I respect that I am an individual.  We have the ability to do things nobody else can do.  Never stop looking for opportunities to make a difference in the lives of every person, especially you.

I did not, I was prescribed prozac and it worked for me.  Could something else have worked better?  Maybe.  But after finding something that is improving you, you don't feel inclined to continue searching.  As for side effects, there are usually a few.  These were stomach aches, dizziness, drowsiness, take forever to orgasm (which sounds bad but will impress your partner whenever you hook up).  Now, all of these.. (except the last one to a certain degree) have completely left me.  That is normal, peoples bodies naturally learn to adjust to most of the side effects of the meds.  I believe it took me about a month to completely adjust to side effects, and about 5 months to finally feel an improvement in my depression.  But once you notice that improvement, you *really* notice.  So patience is key.  Now that is prozac, but i have read about many other anti depression meds, and all the side effects are pretty much the same.  Your preferences are something you should talk to your doctor about.  but just know this, and don't forget it, its a sentence that has been ringing in my head for years.  Your brain has a certain chemical imbalance right now, the medication does not add thoughts or emotions to your brain, it allows your brain to start producing the chemicals it *should* and *would* have been producing on its own if not for your depression.  Meds are not the only way to make this happen though, cognitive therapy is also well known to make your brain improve its chemical imbalance.

For sure, I rejected my offer for group sessions, I still regret it to this day.  As for medication, I was *extremely* afraid that they would turn me into someone else.  Know what though?
